lessons.title: Allocating Binary Memory with ArrayBuffer
lessons.description: ArrayBuffer allocates a fixed block of raw binary memory — the foundation for working with binary data in JavaScript.

sections.heading: What is ArrayBuffer?
paragraphs: An ArrayBuffer is a fixed-length raw binary data buffer. You can't read or write it directly — you must create a typed view to interpret the bytes.
list: Use TypedArrays or DataView to read/write the bytes

codeExamples.heading: Creating an ArrayBuffer
explanation: ArrayBuffer allocates raw memory — no reading or writing directly.
TypedArray views interpret the bytes as specific data types.
Uint8Array treats each byte as an unsigned 8-bit integer (0–255).
The same buffer can have multiple views with different interpretations.

practice.task: Create an ArrayBuffer of 8 bytes and use a Uint8Array view to store the ASCII codes for "Hello!".

keyTakeaways: ArrayBuffer allocates fixed-length raw binary memory.
You must create a TypedArray view to read/write the bytes.
The same buffer can have multiple views with different data type interpretations.
ArrayBuffer is the foundation for binary data in the browser and Node.js.
lessons.challenge: Create an ArrayBuffer and interpret it as both Uint8Array and Int32Array to see how the same bytes look in different formats.

lessons.title: TypedArray Views (Uint8Array, Float64Array)
lessons.description: TypedArrays provide typed views over ArrayBuffers — read and write binary data as specific numeric types.

sections.heading: TypedArray types
list: All TypedArrays share the same API: length, slice, fill, map, etc.

codeExamples.heading: TypedArray operations
explanation: TypedArrays allocate their own ArrayBuffer internally.
They behave like arrays but are fixed-length and type-restricted.
Use TextDecoder to convert bytes to strings.
Different types have different byte sizes and value ranges.

practice.task: Create a Uint8Array from a string using TextEncoder, then decode it back with TextDecoder.
hints: Verify the round-trip produces the original string.

keyTakeaways: TypedArrays provide typed views over binary data.
Different types have different byte sizes and value ranges.
Use TextEncoder/TextDecoder to convert between strings and bytes.
TypedArrays are used in audio processing, image manipulation and network protocols.
lessons.challenge: Build a simple image processor that reads pixel data as Uint8Array and applies a grayscale filter.

lessons.title: DataView Manipulation & Endianness Controls
lessons.description: DataView reads binary data in specific byte orders — essential for network protocols and file formats.

sections.heading: What is DataView?
paragraphs: DataView provides fine-grained control over reading and writing binary data. Unlike TypedArrays, it can read different types from the same buffer and control byte order (endianness).
list: new DataView(buffer, offset, length) — creates a view into a buffer
Read/write specific types at specific offsets
Essential for binary file formats and network protocols

codeExamples.heading: DataView for binary protocols
explanation: DataView reads/writes at specific byte offsets in the buffer.
The boolean parameter controls endianness (byte order).
Big-endian: most significant byte first. Little-endian: least significant first.
Different systems use different endianness — DataView handles both.

practice.task: Use DataView to write your name as individual bytes into an ArrayBuffer, then read them back as a string.

keyTakeaways: DataView provides fine-grained control over binary data access.
Read/write at specific byte offsets with specific data types.
Control endianness for cross-platform binary compatibility.
Essential for parsing binary file formats and network protocols.
lessons.challenge: Parse a BMP image header using DataView to extract width, height and color depth.

lessons.title: String Encoding Conversions via TextEncoder & TextDecoder
lessons.description: Convert between JavaScript strings and binary data using the Encoding API.

sections.heading: TextEncoder and TextDecoder
list: new TextDecoder() — converts Uint8Array back to strings
UTF-8 is the default encoding for both
Essential for working with binary data that represents text

codeExamples.heading: Encoding and decoding strings
explanation: TextEncoder produces UTF-8 bytes — each character may be 1–4 bytes.
Chinese/Japanese characters use 3 bytes in UTF-8.
TextDecoder can handle different encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16, etc.
The byte length differs from the string length for multi-byte characters.

practice.task: Encode a string with special characters to bytes, check the byte length vs string length, then decode it back.

keyTakeaways: TextEncoder converts strings to UTF-8 bytes (Uint8Array).
TextDecoder converts bytes back to strings, supporting multiple encodings.
UTF-8 uses 1–4 bytes per character — byte length differs from string length.
Essential for binary protocols, file I/O and network communication.
lessons.challenge: Build a simple file reader that loads a text file as ArrayBuffer and decodes it to a string using TextDecoder.
